summary: Issue tracker built for coding agents: a dependency-aware task graph stored in Dolt that gives agents lasting memory for long projects.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Beads (the bd command) is a distributed graph issue tracker for AI coding agents. It replaces loose markdown plans with tasks that have dependencies, priorities and owners, stored in a version-controlled Dolt database. Agents ask bd which tasks are ready, claim one, and close it when done, and project memories can be stored and re-injected later.
sixtySeconds.problem: Coding agents lose track of long tasks and plans scattered across markdown files. Beads gives them a structured, persistent task list that survives sessions and merges cleanly across branches.
whoFor: Developers using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Factory
Teams running several agents on one codebase
People tackling long multi-step projects with agents
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for dependency-aware ready-task detection, hash-based IDs that avoid merge conflicts, JSON output for agents and built-in setup for popular agents.

overview: Install the bd CLI once system-wide (Homebrew, npm or the install script); don't clone the repo into your project. Then run bd init in your project.
bd init writes AGENTS.md guidance and installs Claude Code, Codex and Cursor integrations unless you skip them. bd setup claude or bd setup codex refreshes richer instructions.
Data lives in an embedded Dolt database by default; server mode supports several writers, and bd dolt push/pull syncs through your git remote. It is MIT licensed.
